blindSummary:
This state/province is the only jurisdiction in the country to pass laws targeting transgender people as a class and then shield those laws from judicial review. A 2024 education amendment (in force 1 Sep 2025) mandates parental notification/consent before staff use a student's gender-related preferred name or pronouns; a parallel 2024 health statute prohibits puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and a vital-statistics rule was amended. A 2025 law invoked a constitutional override power over all three laws, and after it passed the state/province's senior trial court lifted the injunction that had paused the care ban — a government appeal succeeded, removing the injunction.

These school and healthcare provisions are primarily resident-facing and carry small traveler-facing weight. The more directly relevant signal is the documented street-level pattern in the state/province's main city: a pastor led repeated disruptions of library drag-storytime events from 2023, shouting slurs at parents and children; events were cancelled or postponed as threats escalated. His conviction for harassing a librarian was upheld on appeal, and acquittals on disturbance/mischief were overturned with a new trial ordered; a further breach conviction followed in 2026. The institutional response is mixed-leaning-positive, but the pattern of cancelled public expression events and the government's willingness to override courts constitute a clear escalation in this state/province's posture.

The constitutional override power — described by legal commentators as the nuclear option — signals a government that legislates against trans people and defeats judicial review; combined with the disruption pattern (traveller-facing cancellation of public events), this places this state/province well below every other state/province in the country. The 2021 gender-related homicide rate (0.68/100k, second-highest subnational rate) is a weak proxy only and not trans-specific.

Against the next-worst state/province nationally, this one is materially worse: both used the constitutional override to immunise trans-targeting legislation, but this state/province adds a multi-year, event-level pattern of public disruption at libraries that a visitor could encounter directly. The gap to the country-wide picture reflects that no other state/province has paired legislative targeting with a judicial-override shield and a documented cancellation pattern in one unit.
